SUAS-013 — System Ideographic Source Registry

The structural counterpart of UAX #45: one 16-byte source record, one 12-byte variant link, and a lookup that is a hash and a bounded probe.

SUAS-013 (SISR) is the thirteenth SuperUnicode Architecture Standard and the structural counterpart of UAX #45, the U-source ideograph annex. UAX #45 records an ideograph’s provenance as a string such as UTC-00932, and its status, IDS decomposition, radical-stroke data and first residual stroke count as text interleaved with that string. SISR keeps the identity and closes the architecture around it: two byte-packed tables, a bounded lookup, and a verification surface the compiler must satisfy before it emits a record.

SISR does not re-implement SUAS-009 (SIP). SIP answers what an ideograph is — radical, stroke count, classification, collation seed. SISR answers where it came from and what replaces it. Where both name a fallback, the two tables must agree; the reference tests enforce that invariant.

Why a binary registry

Aspect UAX #45 SISR
Definition A text data file, parsed at run time Two static binary tables, compiled at build time
Identity A string, UTC-00932 A 24-bit authority-local serial; the string is a derived view
Status Narrative text A proven six-bit classification field
Lookup Search the file A hash and a bounded probe — O(1) expected
Fallback A description One canonical target per source form, resolved in O(1)
Failure mode An implementer’s own reconciliation The verifier names the first of fourteen defects

The source record

Six fields, 16 bytes, no padding on any supported ABI. The seeding sketch supplied codepoint, source_id_hash, registry_flags, source_type and reserved; SISR adds source_serial, because a 32-bit hash is an integrity check, not an identity.

typedef struct {
uint32_t codepoint; /* Base SUCS codepoint */
uint32_t source_serial; /* authority-local serial, 1..0xFFFFFF */
uint32_t source_id_hash; /* FNV-1a of the canonical token */
uint16_t registry_flags; /* SISR_SOURCE_* bitfield */
uint8_t source_type; /* suas_sisr_source_type_t */
uint8_t reserved; /* must be zero */
} sisr_source_entry_t;

The identity is the pair (source_type, source_serial). The token is derived: PREFIX- followed by at least five zero-padded decimal digits, widening only above 99999 — so UTC-00932 round-trips exactly and RNUR-00256 needs no special case. source_id_hash is the FNV-1a of that token.

Source Registry class Variant fallback
0x00160100 — RNUR-00256 RNUR set 1, verified —
0x00160101 — RNUR-00257 RNUR set 1, verified 0x00160102
0x00009F8D — UK-00001 historical (UK) 0x00160200 — traditional
0x00009F99 — UTC-00002 historical (UTC) 0x00160201 — simplified
0x0000FA26 — UTC-00932 historical, verified 0x000090FD — compatibility
0x00160300 — CONL-00001 conlang, verified 0x00160301

The variant link

Source identity and glyph preference are different questions, so links live in their own 12-byte table. A codepoint may have a source identity and no fallback, a fallback that is itself a source form, or share a fallback with others.

typedef struct {
uint32_t codepoint; /* the source form */
uint32_t fallback_codepoint; /* the canonical glyph to render */
uint16_t link_flags; /* SISR_LINK_* bitfield */
uint16_t reserved; /* must be zero */
} sisr_variant_link_t;

Eight link bits are assigned: SIMPLIFIED, TRADITIONAL, Z_VARIANT, COMPATIBILITY, REORDERED, APPROXIMATE, REGISTRY and CUSTOM. A link whose flags are zero is rejected, and a self-link is rejected, because an unclassified or reflexive fallback cannot be audited.

Zones and the RNUR decode

A source identity may name only the Bridge plane, the RNUR neography carve-out, or the custom-conscript Native plane. The Control Plane, the trap slots, the Sentinel and ExtSUCS are never source identities. The RNUR set number is the same decode SSP publishes: set = (cp − 0x00160000) >> 8.

Zone Range Source identity?
BRIDGE 0x00000000–0x0010FFFF Yes
SCP 0x00110000–0x0011FFFF No — Control Plane
NATIVE rest of 0x00120000–0x7FFFFFEF Yes — custom conscript space
RNUR 0x00160000–0x0016FFFF Yes — neography
TRAP / SENTINEL / EXTSUCS terminals and plugin space No

Lookup and its cost

Operation Cost
suas_sisr_init_registry O(n) once, n ≤ 256, no allocation
suas_sisr_get_source_entry O(1) expected — one hash and a bounded probe
suas_sisr_fallback_target / _get_variant_link O(1) expected
suas_sisr_is_registered O(1) expected
suas_sisr_format_source_id O(1) — bounded token writer
suas_sisr_validate_table / _links O(n²) worst case — a compiler-time verifier

Verification names the defect

suas_sisr_validate_table returns the first of fourteen named outcomes: a NULL table, a count over capacity, an unordered pair, a duplicate codepoint, a codepoint past the space, an inadmissible codepoint, a bad serial, a bad authority, a reserved or contradictory flag bit, a nonzero reserved byte, a duplicate identity, a stale hash, or a broken link. An empty registry is valid: an implementation with no ideographic sources ships zero records and conforms.

Classification note

The seeding sketch labelled SISR SUTS-006, on the argument that a registry is modular optional compliance. The series owner directed that it be authored as a SUAS standard, so it is registered as SUAS-013, the number immediately after SUAS-012 (SUCD). One element of the SUTS framing survives deliberately: the registry contents are optional version data, so an implementation with no ideographic sources ships an empty registry and remains conformant — while the engine, the layout, the lookup contract and the verification rules are mandatory architecture.

The sketch’s own body cited SUCD as “SUAS-014”. That is stale: SUCD is SUAS-012. SISR is SUAS-013, and SUAS-014 remains unallocated.

Reference implementation: include/suas/suas_sisr.h + src/suas/suas_sisr.c (freestanding C99, no heap), registered in suas_static and in the SSRE registry as a MANDATORY specification.

Source of truth: docs/suas/SUAS-013-sisr.md in the repository.
